key_insight: No single intra-patient 3D multimodal registration method is robust across datasets, and geometric overlap gains can disagree with true multimodal structural alignment.
engineering_relevance: For clinical imaging pipelines, method selection must balance overlap, deformation quality, and cross-modality consistency rather than optimizing only one metric.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based and modern learning-based deformable registration methods, including foundation models.
Compared performance across three datasets spanning synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical cases.
Evaluated with complementary metrics: DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC to capture geometric and image-based alignment.
evidence_signal: The benchmark shows strong variability across anatomies, with learning-based methods doing best on large synthetic data but only limited gains in real pelvic registration.
watch_item: High Dice or low HD95 may hide poor global multimodal correspondence, especially when anatomy-guided methods overfit to segmented regions.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
